reviews.body:
Good work on adding reusable pytest fixtures! Using a temporary SQLite database is a good approach to keep the tests isolated from the production database.

I noticed that CI reports an unused noqa directive (RUF100) on line 14 of tests/conftest.py. Please remove the unnecessary # noqa: E402 and rerun the checks. The Python tests are passing, but the No secrets checks are also failing, so please take a look at those before merging. Thanks!

I checked the test documentation. The test cases are clearly organized, and the expected results are easy to follow. One thing worth checking is whether all nine test cases match the actual tests in tests/test_auth.py, especially the duplicate email constraint test. Also, the No secrets checks are still failing, so please check the CI logs before merging. The Python tests are passing. Thanks!
Soạn

I checked the setup instructions. The steps for installing dependencies and running the test suite are clear. I also like that you mentioned tests use isolated databases and don't require manually starting the Flask server. One thing to verify is that requirements-dev.txt is available in the repository and the commands work from a clean clone. The No secrets checks are still failing, so please investigate those before merging. Thanks!

Adding a separate `requirements-dev.txt` makes sense for M4, since it keeps testing tools separate from the application's runtime dependencies.

One thing I noticed is that this PR only adds the dependency file, while issue #170 also requires updating `docs/SETUP.md` with instructions for running automated tests from a clean clone.

Could you add those instructions to `docs/SETUP.md` or confirm that they will be handled in a separate PR? We should also verify that installing `requirements-dev.txt` and running pytest works without manually starting the Flask server.

I reviewed the Sprint 4 log update. The new section gives a clear overview of the sprint goal, completed work, metrics, retrospective, and follow-up actions. I also appreciate that the story points and velocity are still marked as TBD rather than using unverified figures.

Before merging, please double-check that the recorded issues and completed work match the Sprint 4 Project Board, and update the metrics once they are confirmed. The Python tests are passing, and the documentation change appears straightforward. However, both No secrets committed checks are currently failing, so please investigate the CI logs and resolve those failures before merging.

One more thing: the PR description says Closes #171. Since the sprint issue may still have outstanding tasks, please confirm that all its acceptance criteria are complete before closing it. Thanks! 
Soạn

The testing documentation is well structured, and I appreciate that the missing test coverage is clearly marked instead of being reported as completed.

One concern is that 23 out of 41 test cases are still marked as NOT IMPLEMENTED. Since Section 3 requires every documented test case to have a corresponding pytest test, we need to make sure these are completed through #165–#169 before the final M4 submission.

The mutation test for the 24-hour boundary is useful evidence that the test can detect an actual logic change. Please also keep the test mapping updated as the remaining tests are implemented, so the documentation stays consistent with the code.

Overall, this is a good starting point for M4 testing documentation, but the remaining coverage needs to be tracked carefully.
